stage6.name: Stage 6: Year-Weighted Constructor
stage6.description: Dirichlet-Multinomial with recency-weighted constructor priors. Best calibrated model (LL/race = -59.0). Trained 2015-2025.

stage9.name: Stage 9: Bayesian State-Space
stage9.description: Random walk on driver/constructor log-strengths with Plackett-Luce observations. Best top-3 accuracy (1.59/3). Trained 2015-2025.

composite.name: Composite (2-Model Blend)
composite.description: Equal-weight blend of Stage 6 + Stage 9 probabilities, renormalized.

agent_prediction.name: Agent Forecast (Claude)
agent_prediction.description: Predicted by Claude using web-searched current form, prior-season results, and qualitative judgment.
agent_prediction.rationale: Monaco is a track-position race where qualifying pace and circuit specialism outweigh aggregate season form. The composite model anchors on Antonelli (30.2% P(win)) â€” fair given his four-race winning streak and 43-point championship lead â€” but the quantitative stages have no circuit features and will under-weight Leclerc, who is Ferrari's Monaco home hero and the 2024 Monaco winner. Verstappen's career Monaco record (multiple wins, repeatedly converts front-row starts) makes him the cleanest pick for the third podium slot ahead of Hamilton, whose Canada P2 was attrition-aided. Russell starts in question after his Canada DNF (power unit) and is downgraded into the top-10 tail. McLaren remains a wildcard â€” Norris is the better Monaco bet of the pair but recent reliability and pace dropoff (Norris DNF in Canada, Piastri P11) suggest top-6 at best. Signals from after the Thursday 6/4 on-track running are excluded by user request.
